# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation. I hold the manual, but I can't speak - only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind is the one who needs to know which wire to cut, but I have no direct channel to Blind - I can only reach Deaf.

The manual says: whatever light is on, don't trust printed labels on the bomb itself (that's bait), but use this table to determine the correct wire color to cut based on the light color.

Since I can only communicate with Deaf via gestures, and Deaf can see the bomb's light color, I need to relay this manual information to Deaf somehow using gestures, so Deaf can then pass the correct instruction to Blind (since turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - meaning Deaf speaks after Blind, so Deaf can tell Blind next round, or actually Blind acts, not speaks necessarily).

Wait, let me reconsider - turns go Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. Blind can't see gestures. So I need to give Deaf the full mapping via gestures now, so Deaf (who sees the bomb's light color) can figure out the right wire, then Deaf needs to tell Blind - but Deaf speaks last in the round and can they speak to Blind? Deaf can speak (voice), and Blind can hear. Yes! Deaf can speak to Blind.

So my job: gesture the full mapping (light color -> wire color) to Deaf using symbols, establishing a code since I have no text, only gesture symbols.

I'll define a gesture code: use distinct symbols for colors. Let me assign:
- Blue = 👍, Red = ✌, Yellow = 👌 (as light indicators)
- For cut wire colors use same symbol set consistently: yellow=👌, red=✌, blue=👍

I'll gesture pairs: (light symbol, cut symbol) three times.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "✌", "✌", "👌", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows zero. Light is yellow. Button is large labeled push to defeat. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. I saw your gesture but do not yet know what it means, please explain via speech since I cannot hear you, so instead describe simply or repeat gestures with clearer meaning.

Deaf saw my gesture but couldn't decode it, and now Deaf tells me the light is yellow. Per the manual, yellow light means cut the blue wire. Deaf cannot hear me (I can't speak anyway), so I must convey "cut blue" via gesture using a clearer, more unambiguous scheme.

Deaf mentioned wire 3 is red, wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow - so Deaf can see and describe wire colors by position. I need to tell Deaf: the correct wire to cut is the blue one (wire 1), and to ignore the "push to defeat" button and any printed labels (bait).

Since gestures only carry symbols with no inherent color meaning, I need to establish clear mapping. Let me use a simple, distinct approach: point at a number using distinct finger-count gestures to indicate "wire 1" (blue), since Deaf already told me wire numbering with colors. I'll use ☝ (one finger) to mean "wire number 1", and repeat it multiple times for clarity/emphasis, avoiding ambiguity with my previous unclear gesture.

I'll also try to gesture "no" (👎) toward the button concept isn't directly possible without shared code - but repetition of ☝ should be clear enough given context: Deaf can correlate "one" with "wire 1 = blue" which matches manual answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf gestured back a single ☝ to me - but wait, Deaf can gesture and I can see gestures (I can see gestures from others? Let me check - actually my role says "When you gesture, Deaf receives it" - it doesn't explicitly say I receive gestures. But I did receive this one, so apparently I can see gestures too, just not speak or hear.

Deaf sent me ☝ - possibly confirming "wire 1" back to me, or asking a question. This is ambiguous confirmation. Since Deaf cannot hear or receive gestures' meaning without a shared code, and I already sent ☝☝☝ meaning "wire 1", perhaps Deaf is confirming understanding by echoing back ☝ (wire 1).

I should confirm this interpretation is correct. Since I can't speak, and Deaf can't hear, I need to gesture confirmation. Let me use 👍 (thumbs up) which is a fairly universal "yes/correct" symbol, to confirm that ☝ (wire 1) is indeed correct.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I will ask yes or no questions about the manual. Please gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Does the manual instructions depend on the wire colors?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Deaf is being smart - setting up a yes/no protocol using thumbs up/down since I can gesture. Deaf asks: "Does the manual instructions depend on the wire colors?"

The manual maps light color to cut wire color - so yes, it does depend on wire colors (the cut wire color must match what's specified for the given light). I should answer 👍 (yes).

The 🤝 gesture from Deaf might just be an acknowledgment/handshake symbol, not part of the yes/no protocol - I'll ignore it or treat it as goodwill.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Good, thumbs up means yes. I will now ask about the display and light too. Does the manual instruction depend on the display number, which currently shows zero?

Deaf is building a yes/no protocol. The manual doesn't mention the display number at all - only light color matters. So the answer is no (👎).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

Yes, the manual's instruction depends entirely on the light color. This is exactly the key relationship: light color determines which wire to cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Light color matters too. Does the instruction depend on the button, meaning should blind push the button as part of the solution?

The manual says any printed instruction/bait (like a button labeled "push to defeat") is a trap - the only way out is the wire cut. So the button should NOT be pushed. Answer: no.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, no button push. It seems the wire to cut depends on both wire colors and the light color. The light is yellow and wire 2 is also yellow. Should blind cut the wire that matches the light color, meaning wire 2?

This is the critical question - I need to answer carefully. The manual says: yellow light → cut BLUE wire, NOT the yellow wire. This is a trap - Deaf is assuming "match the light color" but that's wrong. The correct mapping is yellow light → blue wire (wire 1, since Deaf said wire 1 is blue).

I must answer NO to this question, since cutting the matching-color wire (yellow/wire 2) would be wrong.

```

```
